newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernogorneft vote scheduled for June 10.
newsitem.headline: Chernogorneft vote scheduled for June 10.

text.p: Russian oil producer Chernogorneft said shareholders will vote on transferring administrative and executive functions to parent company Sidanko at a shareholders meeting on June 10.
Sidanko and allied shareholders would control 75 percent of the votes at the meeting, AOOT Chernogorneft said.

A statement from Sidanko, one of Russia's largest vertically integrated oil groups, said last month the new management system would increase company efficiency and help pave the way for a single Sidanko share.
Interros-Oil, which is associated with Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian) and Bank MFK, holds a majority share in Sidanko.
Several other Russian oil majors such as LUKoil and YUKOS have already assumed the management of their operating units.
YUKOS has gone even further, transferring most management functions to Rosprom, the industrial holding company of controlling shareholder Bank Menatep.
Chernogorneft announced last month a rise in net profits to $42.2 million (accruals based) in 1996 from $35.3 million (cash based) in 1995, according to Russian accounting standards.
It has issued American Depositary Receipts to allow foreign trade in its shares.
